page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, catchword at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Coloss. 1. 20. Et pacem per sanguinem crucis ejus facta placuit Patri per eum reconciliare sibi omnia, tum quae in terra, tum quae in coelis. Itaque vos quondam abalienatos & hostes, mente operibus malis intenta, nunc sane reconciliavit, in corpore illo carnis suae per mortem, &c. hoc est, Quandoquidem Deo Patri visum est per illum Filium suum, totam creaturarum universitatem inhabitare, ac plenitudinem omnium suorum in illo residere: Itaque placuit eidem Patri per sanguinem CHRISTI in cruce effusum, universalem pacem, inter Angelos & Homines sancire, & utrosque inter se reconciliare, hoc est, tum eos, qui in terra, tum eos qui in coelis sunt, ad suam ipsius gloriam.

Ne verò putemus tantum hic agi de dissidio inter Gentes & Judaeos, interque Angelos & Homines: dicimur alibi Pacem erga Deum consequuti per fidem in CHRISTUM. Roman. 5. vers. 1, quia nimirum Pater in Christo, ut Sponsore nostro, acquiescit. Matth. 3. v. 17. Pater ipse dicit: Hic est filius meus ille dilectus, in quo acquiesce. Hic enim est, qui calcat lacum vini furoris & irae Dei. Apoçal, 5. v. 15.

page.notes: The running head "CAP. IV. SECT. II." is printed. The bold, slanted "264" at the top right looks like a later hand rather than print, so it is left out; a small mark at the top centre is unclear and also left out. The catchword "Hinc" is printed at the right foot. Italic and roman boundaries in the Latin passage were judged from the scan and may be slightly off. "Apoçal" is copied as printed, with the cedilla-like letter. Possible misreading: "acquiesce" in the Matthew quotation, where the scan shows long-s forms.
